grammar_only: The specimens were cooled from 130 °C to 20 °C at 4 °C/min, and their mass was recorded before immersion. Each specimen was then immersed in toluene for 24 h; the resulting mass changes do not, by themselves, establish network degradation.
paragraph_revision: In five separately prepared devices measured at 22 °C, the mean sensitivity increased from 0.8 to 1.3 kPa−1 after surface treatment over the pressure range 0–2 kPa; no statistical hypothesis test was performed. Optical imaging showed a larger contact area under load after treatment, with no resolvable change in film thickness. These observations are consistent with a contribution from increased contact area, but they do not establish it as the sole cause of the sensitivity increase: mechanical modulus was not measured, leaving changes in bulk stiffness as a possible explanation. A matched-modulus control could help distinguish these explanations, but has not yet been performed. The sensor retained 94% of its initial response after 200 loading cycles at 1 kPa, demonstrating response retention under these conditions without establishing long-term durability.
preserve_voice: The interface, rather than the bulk film, set the limit on adhesion. We reached this conclusion by changing the surface treatment while keeping the film formulation and cure unchanged. Untreated specimens separated at the interface; treated specimens failed within the film. The result does not identify the bonding mechanism, but it locates the weakest link under the conditions tested. For this system, that distinction is enough to guide the next experiment.
